item.speaker: sam
item.prompt: Sam's notes on the history of computer vision. One line is wrong - show Sam the passage that proves it.

statements.text: Hubel & Wiesel's study showed that simple and complex cells respond to light orientation and movement.
statements.why: Correct, this is exactly what the passage describes about simple and complex cells.

sourceRefs.quote: Complex cells: Response to light orientation and movement

statements.text: Marr's theory describes vision moving from raw perceived intensities toward a full 3-D model.
statements.why: Correct, the passage lists the input image's perceived intensities as the starting representation.

statements.text: Viola & Jones studied simple, complex, and hypercomplex brain cells to build their face detection algorithm.
statements.why: This mixes up two different milestones: the brain-cell study was done by Hubel & Wiesel, not Viola & Jones, who are credited with face detection instead.

statements.text: CNNs were not invented overnight; they came out of decades of incremental research.
statements.why: Correct, the passage explicitly states CNNs were not invented overnight.

hints: One note mixes up the brain-cell researchers with the face-detection researchers — which passage names who actually did what?
